title: Will at least one paper published in Nature, Science, or Cell list an AI system as a formally credited author before January 1, 2030?
reasons: The live page shows 80% and 18 forecasters but omits the full resolution criteria, so verification is incomplete and API collection is unavailable. Any credited author in Nature, Science, or Cell would be weaker than actual primary-authored publication, but our binding assumes clause instead measures capability with the authorship-policy barrier removed. That capability does not imply real-world formal credit, while merely crediting an AI does not establish its independent conception, analysis and writing; thus the visible event would not bound the actual framework milestone.
collection_status: no_authenticated_api_access; complete_criteria_unavailable

title: Will an AI system be credited as the lead author of a paper in Nature or Science before 1 January 2030?
reasons: The market requires actual first/lead/primary credit in a published Nature or Science paper but does not require the AI to originate the question, design and analyse the research, and write it without human intellectual contributions. Our milestone assumes away the journal-authorship ban, whereas this unconditional market can remain NO because of that policy even when the capability milestone is met. Conversely, editorial credit alone could produce YES without the required AI-only research; neither implication holds, and three bettors also make this exceptionally thin.

title: Will there be a one-person unicorn by 2030?
reasons: A billion-dollar valuation is neither necessary nor sufficient for $10M recurring revenue with less than ten total human operating hours per week averaged over a quarter. The market explicitly permits operating contractors and its 2026 update also accepts $1.8B in sales as valuation evidence, neither of which enforces recurring revenue or the oversight cap. Our qualifying business could be worth much less than $1B, while a qualifying unicorn could employ substantial contractor labour and have no recurring revenue.

title: Will a robot be created that is capable of passing Steve Wozniak's "The Coffee Test" before 2029?

Its added 20-minute limit also excludes a slower, independently verified, unaided success that satisfies our milestone. Thus a developer-selected demonstration could satisfy the market without our event, while our event need not satisfy the market; the mixed requirements prevent both weaker and stronger classifications.

title: Will there be a fusion reactor generating electricity commercially by the end of 2035?
reasons: Three consecutive months of net electricity export under commercial operation to a public grid entails grid connection, commercial electricity sales and net-positive energy operation as required here. The market imposes no three-month minimum and does not require the same explicit net-electrical accounting, so a shorter commercial delivery can resolve YES before our milestone. It is a lower-bound event and supplies P(our milestone by 2035-12-31) ≤ 0.3678032316, not an estimate of our milestone probability; eleven bettors warrant a thin-market warning rather than automatic rejection.

title: Will there be a major shift in cancer survival rates by 2030?
reasons: The market asks for a roughly twenty-point change in five-year survival across all cancers, with no settled source, baseline or resident-population definition; our test is an absolute 80% ten-year net survival level for solid tumours in a whole population of at least 50M. Five-year improvement does not entail the ten-year threshold, and our frontier could meet that threshold without the specified all-cancer change. A creator update moves closing to 2035 without cleanly reconciling the title’s 2030 event cutoff, adding a resolution ambiguity rather than a usable bound.

title: When will the average five-year survival rate of all cancers exceed 95%?
reasons: The live page displays a February 2057 estimate and twenty forecasters but does not expose the full population/statistic/resolution rules, so this is unverifiable. From the visible title, 95% five-year survival across all cancers does not guarantee 80% ten-year net survival for solid tumours, because deaths after year five can still be substantial. Conversely, 80% ten-year solid-tumour survival does not require 95% five-year all-cancer survival; the relation would be reject, not stronger, even before the unresolved geography and averaging rules.

title: Will glioblastoma (an aggressive brain cancer) have a 5-year relative survival rate greater than 15% in the US in 2035?
reasons: A US glioblastoma five-year relative survival point estimate above 15% is compatible with poor overall solid-tumour survival, so it does not imply our aggregate ten-year threshold. Our aggregate can exceed 80% while a small difficult subtype remains below 15%, and the qualifying frontier need not be the US, so our milestone does not imply this event either. Resolution uses the 2035 CBTRUS report’s earlier diagnosis cohorts, with discretionary substitution or interpolation, not a 2035 treatment cohort or an independent metastatic-cancer requirement.

title: Global CO2 Emissions Peak Year
reasons: The live extract shows a November 2031 estimate and a moderator clarification that the metric is CO2 including land-use change, but not the complete resolution criteria or a current forecaster count. A CO2 peak need not occur before the peak of all GHGs, since non-CO2 gases can offset CO2 changes in either direction. Nor is the physical CO2 peak date the date when an all-GHG inventory establishes a peak at least three years back with the latest year at least 1% lower; the visible relation would be reject, and API access remains blocked.

A single annual fall in 2025–2029 need not establish our three-year-old all-GHG peak and 1% reduction; in the other direction, an earlier qualifying peak need not produce a fall specifically within this window. If the scope and time window matched, a mere fall could be weaker than confirmation, but those mismatches prevent that implication here.

Its allowance for unspecified natural removals and a NO on significant delay or retraction also fails to enforce our durable anthropogenic accounting; neither implication holds.
